content.text: Most tutorials about building a [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/digital-product-payment-solutions-west-africa-what-actually-2|Digital Product]] store focus on the storefront. The storefront is the last thing you should configure. The backend is what makes the store work — and the backend is what most creators get wrong when they try to build without a clear sequence. In Stack 01, Google Apps Script serves as the backend Web App — it receives the NOW[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-gateways-cameroon-digital-products-one-afternoon-fast|payment]]s webhook, validates the signature, confirms the transaction on-chain, logs the order to Google Sheets, and sends the delivery email via Gmail. In Stack 02, Cloudflare Workers replaces Apps Script with a faster, more scalable serverless backend that integrates natively with Supabase for order storage and Resend for email delivery. Configure the backend first, set the webhook endpoint URL in NOW[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/tron-usdt-payments-digital-products-explained-digital-creators-13|COREMERCH guide to payments]] second, build the storefront third, and test on mainnet fourth.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

Stack 01 — the Sovereign Starter Stack — uses GitHub Pages for storefront hosting, Google Apps Script as the backend Web App, Google Sheets as the order database, Google Drive for product file storage, and Gmail for delivery email. The entire stack costs nothing per month. Google Apps Script runs in response to webhook events from NOWPayments, validates the payment, logs the order to Google Sheets, generates a receipt, and sends a Gmail delivery email with a Google Drive shared link. The daily limits on the free tier are adequate for most creators at the early and growth stages.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Stack 02 — the Edge Commerce Stack — uses Cloudflare Pages for storefront hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend webhook handling, Supabase for order storage, Cloudflare R2 for product file delivery, and Resend for transactional email. The entire stack costs nothing per month up to significant volume thresholds — Cloudflare Workers provides 100,000 requests per day free, Supabase provides 500MB of PostgreSQL storage free, Cloudflare R2 provides 10GB storage and zero egress fees free, and Resend provides 3,000 emails per month free. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are configured during COREMERCH deployment.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

The NOWPayments configuration sequence is the same regardless of which stack you are deploying. Create a NOWPayments account — no KYC required, no document upload, no bank account needed. Navigate to the wallet settings and add the wallet addresses for each cryptocurrency you want to accept. USDT on Tron and Bitcoin are the practical starting point for most creators in restricted markets. Generate an API key from the NOWPayments dashboard. Set the webhook endpoint URL in the NOWPayments IPN settings pointing to your Cloudflare Worker or Apps Script Web App. Set the webhook secret key — a string you generate that both NOWPayments and your backend know.

Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Testing before promotion is not optional — it is the step that determines whether your store functions correctly under real conditions before real buyers encounter it. The test sequence has four steps. First: deploy the backend and confirm the webhook endpoint returns a valid response to a test HTTP POST. Second: configure the storefront and confirm the checkout displays correctly on desktop and mobile. Third: complete a real mainnet transaction with a small amount of actual crypto. Fourth: check your order database and confirm the order was logged correctly, the delivery email arrived, and the download link works.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your store grows, you'll need to scale your infrastructure to meet increasing demand. The Edge Commerce Stack is designed to support this growth, with Cloudflare Pages and Workers providing a robust, scalable foundation. By monitoring your store's performance and optimizing your configuration as needed, you can ensure a seamless experience for customers, even at high volumes of traffic and sales.

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.

For a hassle-free deployment experience, consider the Edge Commerce Stack, available for $197 at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. This solution includes everything you need to get your store live, from Cloudflare Pages and Workers to NOWPayments integration and automated delivery of digital products.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your digital store on Cloudflare Pages, follow these steps: set up your Cloudflare account, create a NOWPayments account, configure your store's frontend and backend, integrate NOWPayments with Cloudflare Workers, deploy your store on Cloudflare Pages, and test your payment pipeline. With these steps complete, you can start processing transactions and selling your digital products to customers around the world.
